title: Bo's Very Important Tiny Post Office
synopsis: Bo opens a pretend post office at the Doorway Tree with drawings, slipper wheels and a basket that keeps all the real letters.
continuity_state: Before: Button Town has been invented; Tess has a blue-circle visitor ticket inside the yellow map; Nori still owns three pebbles in her pouch. After: Grandma Fern brings a shallow basket and paper, all returned home afterward; friends make three letter drawings (tilted lantern, blue door, yellow boots with ripples). Nori keeps all three pebbles and agrees to deliver Rill his card later. A brown envelope with the three drawings stays at Blue Door Cottage.

related_resources.reason: Nori expresses a simple preference over her own belonging; the social-development guidance concerns emerging peer interaction, not a tested effect of this scene.
Children reuse a real basket and imaginary cart in role-play; the AAP clinical report discusses make-believe play in general.
